title: Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation
abstract: arXiv:2608.19611v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM reasoning is stochastic, and so understanding a model requires grappling with the distribution of reasoning chains that it might produce for a given question, i.e., its uncertainty. Resampling-based analyses characterize this distribution, revealing which steps of a rollout determine how the model arrives at its answer. However, a major limitation of these approaches is that resampling text sequences at every token or sentence in a reasoning chain is very costly. Our work strives to make resampling analysis more computationally efficient, while also shedding light on an important scientific question: what is the right statistical model for explaining uncertainty dynamics in text generation? We show that when resampling many reasoning chains, uncertainty dynamics converge to stable patterns, and noise is largely an artifact of sampling rather than an LLM's sensitivity to each individual token or reasoning step. translated_title: 分叉加速：高效估计文本生成中的不确定性动态
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型的推理具有随机性，因此理解一个模型需要处理其对给定问题可能产生的推理链分布，即其不确定性。基于重采样的分析刻画了这一分布，揭示了在生成过程中哪些步骤决定了模型如何得出答案。然而，这些方法的一个主要局限是，在推理链中每个标记或句子处重采样文本序列的成本非常高。我们的工作旨在使重采样分析在计算上更高效，同时揭示一个重要的科学问题：解释文本生成中不确定性动态的正确统计模型是什么？我们表明，当重采样多个推理链时，不确定性动态会收敛到稳定模式，而噪声主要来自采样的伪影，而非模型对每个单独标记或推理步骤的敏感性。我们开发了一种统计方法来实现这一目标。
tldr: 本文提出了一种高效的重采样分析方法，揭示了文本生成中不确定性动态的稳定模式，并表明噪声主要源于采样而非模型对单个标记的敏感性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an efficient resampling analysis method that reveals stable patterns in uncertainty dynamics of text generation, showing that noise mainly arises from sampling rather than model sensitivity to individual tokens.
